chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb al-Maythami, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام say: There is no harm for the one performing tamattu' if he does not enter ihram on the night of al-Tarwiyah; whenever it becomes possible for him, so long as he does not fear missing the two standing places.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: the two standing places, referring to the major hajj stations
key_terms.فَوْتَ: missing or failing to catch in time
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the night before the eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah, a known hajj time marker
key_terms.يُحْرِمْ: to enter into the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Until when may a pilgrim performing tamattu' delay entering ihram without missing hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the timing of entering ihram for one performing hajj al-tamattu'. It states that delaying ihram beyond the night of al-Tarwiyah is permissible, as long as the pilgrim does not fear missing the essential rites of 'Arafat and al-Mash'ar.
